tagline: Across the Continental Divide, a wagon stop and a copper town
intro: WYO 70 climbs through the Medicine Bow National Forest to cross Battle Pass at 9,955 feet. Travel Wyoming presents the paved Battle Pass Scenic Byway as a drive over the Sierra Madre, with ghost towns, a lake overlook and quaking aspens along the journey. The pass is a seasonal crossing, closed in winter.

An earlier wagon road linked Encampment with the Ferris-Haggarty mine, and Battle grew as a resting stop on it in 1898. A sixteen-mile tramway bypassed Battle in 1902; by 1905 the settlement was a ghost town. The highway number itself has changed in scope: between the 1940s and 1960s, WYO 70 identified only the western stretch from the former Colorado State Highway 129 connection to Baggs. The present highway continues across the mountains to Riverside. The modern highway gained its byway designation from the Wyoming Highway Commission on November 15, 2012.

Drive east from Baggs through Dixon and Savery, then across the brief Colorado section at Slater before entering the national forest. West of the Continental Divide, the Battle Lake turnout offers a view of the lake and an Edison monument. The highway crosses the pass and descends toward Encampment, then ends at WYO 230 in Riverside.

moments.title: Battle Lake overlook
moments.text: A turnout two miles west of the Continental Divide overlooks Battle Lake and a monument to Thomas A. Edison. Travel Wyoming records his vacation here in 1878. The lake belongs to a wider drive through the Sierra Madre mountains of the Medicine Bow National Forest.
moments.notice: The turnout overlooks Battle Lake and a monument to Thomas A. Edison.

moments.title: Battle
moments.text: Battle was a resting stop on the wagon road between the Ferris-Haggarty mine and Encampment. Founded in 1898, it had a post office that operated until 1905. Its place on the route changed in 1902, when a sixteen-mile tramway was completed that bypassed the town. By 1905 it had become a ghost town. The community and Old Battle mining site lie near the summit of Battle Pass. The tram carried ore across the Continental Divide to the smelter built near Encampment in 1902, linking the mountain mine directly with its processing works.

moments.title: Encampment
moments.text: Copper ore once crossed the Continental Divide on a sixteen-mile aerial tram to reach the smelter near Encampment. Built in 1902, the smelter initially made matte, an intermediate copper product; a 1903 upgrade enabled it to produce blister copper. A water turbine powered the refining blowers, fed through a wooden pipe from the South Fork of the Encampment River four miles away. Fires damaged the operation in 1906, and the company was bankrupt by 1910. The smelter buildings have all been removed. The Grand Encampment Museum interprets local mining, ranching and logging through historic buildings and objects.

practical: Battle Lake overlook: WYO 70 over Battle Pass closes in winter, November to April. (checked 2026-10-11)
